learning_outcomes.text: Understanding and mastery of the basic concepts of the general laws of mechanics, thermodynamics, fields and waves, and electromagnetism, and their application to solving engineering problems.

syllabus_topics: The Concept of a Field. Scalar and Vector Fields
Forces. Resultant Force Calculation. Equivalent Force Systems
Moment of a Force. Resultant Moment
Moments of Inertia Calculation. Radius of Gyration. Product of Inertia
Equilibrium Conditions. Free-Body Diagram. Reaction Force Calculation
Position, Velocity and Acceleration Vectors. Equation of the Trajectory
Linear Momentum. Conservation of Linear Momentum
Angular Momentum. Conservation of Angular Momentum
Work Done by a Force and Power
Dynamics of a System of Particles
Motion of the Centre of Mass
Linear Momentum Theorem. Conservation of Linear Momentum
Collisions. Coefficient of Restitution. Elastic and Inelastic Collisions
Kinetic Energy of a System of Particles. Work–Energy Theorem. Conservation of the Total Energy of a System of Particles
Planar Motion of a Rigid Body
Equations of Motion for a Rigid Body: Translation and Rotation
Thermodynamics: Concepts and Definitions. Ideal Gas
Equilibrium States. Quasi-Static Processes and Reversible Processes
teaching_methods: Use of computer-based calculation, visualisation or simulation tools
assessment_rules: The final grade is numerical, with 0-4.9 being Fail, 5.0-6.9 Pass, 7.0-8.9 Good, and 9.0-10 Excellent. Students must obtain a minimum mark of 5.0 in the final examination for other components to be combined. Attendance at practical activities is compulsory, and submission of all practical activity evidence (SE2) is essential; an average mark of at least 5.0 in SE2 is also required to pass, otherwise the module is failed. A minimum mark of 4.0 in application exercises (SE11) is necessary for the final mark calculation, with a weighted average of at least 5.0 required to pass the module. Missing more than 25% of face-to-face classes without valid reason may bar a student from sitting the ordinary examination.
